svg.title: A child with ataxia: localize it (hemisphere for limb ataxia, vermis for truncal ataxia), then sort the three most common causes (intoxication, acute postinfectious cerebellar ataxia, brain tumour) from the can't-miss causes (stroke or hemorrhage, meningitis or encephalitis, brain tumour) by the history; each column says whether to image and what to do

svg.text: Child with ataxia: a SIGN, not a diagnosis

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: cerebellar HEMISPHERE → limbs: over- or undershoots, clumsy · VERMIS → trunk: can't sit, wide-based gait

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: also from vestibular disease (vertigo, vomiting) or weakness, sensory or position-sense loss

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: IMAGE (MRI preferred, CT more accessible) if: ANY other neurologic finding · SUBACUTE course · TRAUMA
